intro.h2: Two former teachers running a boutique design-build firm
paragraphs: VanderBeken Remodel has offered kitchen remodeling in Marysville, WA and across Snohomish County since 2007, from its base on State Avenue. Ron and Jennifer VanderBeken run a family-owned, boutique design-build firm, so design and construction stay under one roof with a single point of contact from the first call to the final walkthrough.

Both owners came from teaching, and they guide clients through each decision the same way. Before production starts you receive concept drawings, 3D renderings, a detailed scope of work and a fixed investment price. During the build a dedicated project manager and a real-time project system keep you informed.

services.h2: Design-build services for Snohomish County homes

items.name: Kitchen Remodeling
items.blurb: Layout, cabinetry, countertops and lighting designed around how you cook and gather, with trades, lead times and materials scheduled ahead. Local material sourcing and careful cabinet and countertop installs mean less waste. VanderBeken kitchens won a 2025 BIAW Excellence in Remodeling Award in the $75,001 to $140,000 class.

image.alt: Modern blue kitchen remodel in Snohomish, WA with a statement waterfall stone countertop, white upper cabinets and a round marble table

items.name: Bathroom Remodeling
items.blurb: Powder rooms, three-quarter baths and full en-suites, from spa-like primary baths with soaking tubs and heated floors to walk-in showers built for aging in place. Two VanderBeken baths won 2025 BIAW Excellence in Remodeling Awards, one under $35,000 and one in the $60,001 to $80,000 range.

image.alt: Lake Stevens primary bathroom with a curbless glass shower, linear drain, marble-look wall tile and freestanding soaking tub

items.name: Universal Design
items.blurb: Certified Aging-in-Place Specialists plan curbless showers, wider doorways, non-slip floors, lever handles, adjustable-height counters and first-floor living spaces. The goal is a home that works for every age and ability without looking clinical. The firm won the 2025 REX Award for Universal Design Excellence.

image.alt: Universal design kitchen with wood cabinets, wall ovens at an easy reach height, a wide white island and a long window wall

items.name: Whole Home and Historic Renovation
items.blurb: Open floor plans, additions, basements and full gut remodels, planned as one project. For older homes in North Everett and Edmonds, the team connects owners with local historic societies, architectural historians and conservators, and sources period-appropriate materials. A 2021 BIAW award covered historic work.

image.alt: Whole home remodel living room with green velvet sofas, built-in wood bookshelves and a tiled fireplace insert

why_choose_us.h2: The VanderBeken difference in four facts

items.title: One fixed investment price
items.text: An advanced estimating system produces a fixed investment price with your drawings and scope, before production begins, so the cost of the remodel is settled up front.

items.title: Two years of coverage
items.text: Every project gets a thorough walkthrough, follow-up visits at 90 days and 12 months, and a two-year warranty on the work.

items.title: Certified owners
items.text: Ron is a BIAW Certified Builder, a NAHB Certified Aging in Place Specialist and RRP certified. Jennifer holds the same builder and CAPS credentials plus NAHB Certified Green Professional.

items.title: Award-winning work
items.text: 2021 MBA Remodeler of the Year, 2024 Everett Herald Best of Snohomish County, a 2018 Chrysalis Award for a kitchen, and REX and BIAW awards for kitchens, baths and universal design.

about.h2: Ron and Jennifer VanderBeken, builders by family and training
about.text: Ron VanderBeken found his love of building while working construction jobs as a student at Seattle Pacific University. After years of teaching and work in custom home building, he became a project manager for a custom home builder in 1998. Jennifer grew up in the trade: her father and grandfather were Seattle-area home builders, and she cleaned job sites as a child. After a career as an elementary school teacher, she joined Ron to launch VanderBeken Remodel in 2007. Ron is co-owner and general manager, and Jennifer is co-owner and operations manager.

steps.title: Walkthrough and follow-ups

service_area.h2: Six Snohomish County cities, and projects beyond
service_area.text: VanderBeken Remodel is based at 306 State Avenue in Marysville and names six areas it serves: Edmonds, Everett, Marysville, Mill Creek, Mukilteo and Snohomish. Its portfolio and reviews also include projects in Lake Stevens, Monroe, Lynnwood and Camano Island. Historic renovation work focuses on North Everett and Edmonds, where older homes need extra care and local review.

items.q: What is design-build, and why does it matter for my kitchen?
items.a: Design-build puts designers, architects and the general contractor on one team. Instead of hiring a designer, then collecting bids and acting as the go-between, you work with a single point of contact. The budget and buildability are considered from the first sketch, which helps avoid the overruns and delays of design-bid-build.

items.q: Will I know the full price before work starts?
items.a: Yes. During the Development phase VanderBeken prepares concept drawings, 3D renderings, a detailed scope of work and a fixed investment price, using an advanced estimating system. You see the complete picture before production begins, which is meant to give you control and predictability over the cost of the remodel.

Every remodel comes with a two-year warranty. After the final walkthrough, where any concerns are addressed, the team follows up at 90 days and again at 12 months to make sure everything is still performing and meeting the firm's standards. You also keep your dedicated project manager as a contact.

items.q: Can you make a bathroom accessible without it looking institutional?
items.a: Yes. Ron and Jennifer are Certified Aging in Place Specialists, and the firm won the 2025 REX Award for Universal Design Excellence. One Lake Stevens client had a 1981 main bath turned into an ADA bath that, in her words, does not look or feel like it.

items.q: Can I bring my own architect or designer?
items.a: Sometimes. Clients occasionally ask to bring their own architect or interior designer, and VanderBeken evaluates each request individually. The team wants to be sure it can coordinate well with them and still deliver the service and results it promises, so raise it during your first call or office visit.

final_cta.text: Call (425) 870-8123 to talk with Ron and Jennifer's team about your kitchen, bath or whole-home project and set up an office visit.
